body: A Day on Site: Behind the Scenes with Our Crew
Every finished building is the result of thousands of small decisions made on site. Here’s what a typical day looks like for the Decode crew.
Each day starts with a short safety briefing and a walk through the plan: which trades are on site, what deliveries are expected, and which areas are off-limits.
Our site managers coordinate trades, check quality as work progresses, and keep clients updated. Small issues get solved the same day, so they never turn into big delays.
How to Choose the Right Contractor for Your Project

The contractor you choose shapes every part of your project — the budget, the schedule, and the quality of the finished space. Taking a little extra time up front to vet your options can save you months of frustration later.

Start with the basics: a valid license, proper insurance, and a track record of similar projects. Ask for references from recent clients and, where possible, visit a completed job to see the workmanship for yourself.
How will the project be scheduled? Who will be on site each day? How are changes and unexpected costs handled? A good contractor answers clearly and puts the important details in writing.

Be cautious of unusually low bids, pressure to sign quickly, requests for large upfront payments, or vague contracts. Clear communication from the very first conversation is one of the best signs you’ve found the right partner.
Permits & Inspections: What You Need Before You Build
Permits can feel like paperwork for its own sake, but they exist to make sure your building is safe, legal, and insurable. Knowing what’s required up front keeps your project moving.
Structural changes, additions, electrical, plumbing, and mechanical work usually require permits. Cosmetic updates like painting or new flooring often don’t — but always check your local rules.

Inspectors visit at key stages — foundations, framing, services, and final completion — to confirm the work meets code. Your contractor should schedule these and be on site to walk the inspector through the work.
Residential vs. Commercial Construction: Key Differences
Building a family home and delivering an office block share the same fundamentals, but the process, scale, and rules around them are very different.

Commercial projects face stricter codes for fire safety, accessibility, and occupancy, along with more inspections along the way. Residential builds are simpler to permit, though local rules still apply.

Commercial work typically involves larger teams, specialist trades, and longer schedules, with budgets to match. Residential projects move faster but are more personal — design decisions often evolve as the homeowner sees the space take shape.

Sustainability has moved from a nice-to-have to a core part of how buildings are designed and delivered. Clients, cities, and building codes are all pushing the industry toward smarter, lower-impact construction.
Recycled steel, low-carbon concrete, responsibly sourced timber, and low-VOC finishes are becoming standard choices. They reduce a building’s footprint without compromising strength or durability.
High-performance insulation, smart glazing, heat pumps, and on-site solar help buildings use less energy for their entire lifetime — lowering running costs as well as emissions.
Top 5 Things to Know Before Starting a Home Renovation

Renovating your home is exciting — but it can quickly become overwhelming without the right preparation. Whether you’re remodeling a kitchen, updating your bathroom, or planning a full home makeover, being informed ahead of time will save you time, stress, and money. Here are the top 5 things you should know before starting your home renovation.

One of the biggest renovation mistakes is underestimating the costs. Get a detailed estimate, and always plan for unexpected expenses by adding 10–20% to your budget. This will give you peace of mind if something unexpected pops up — like plumbing issues or structural repairs.

Before you contact a contractor or pick up a hammer, take the time to understand exactly what you want from the renovation. Are you improving functionality, boosting resale value, or creating your dream space? Clear goals will guide the design and budget process and help your contractor deliver the results you expect.

Depending on the size and scope of your renovation, you may need permits. Skipping this step could result in fines or complications when selling your home later. Your contractor should help you handle permits, but it’s smart to educate yourself on local regulations too.

Do your homework before hiring anyone. Look for licensed, insured professionals with good reviews and relevant experience. Ask to see past work, check references, and make sure you’re comfortable with their communication style and timeline.

Even small renovations can disrupt your daily routine. Noise, dust, and temporary loss of spaces like kitchens or bathrooms are common. Make a plan for how you’ll live around the work — whether that means eating out, staying elsewhere, or setting up a temporary kitchen.

GreenTech Headquarters is a 120,000 sq ft corporate campus built for a renewable energy company that wanted its building to reflect its mission. The design prioritizes daylight, flexible workspaces, and low-carbon construction throughout.

The seven-storey building features a curved high-performance facade, a central atrium that draws natural light deep into the floor plates, and open-plan workspaces that can be reconfigured as teams grow. Biophilic design brings planting into every floor.

As design-and-build contractor, we coordinated architects, MEP engineers, and sustainability consultants from concept through commissioning. Our team managed procurement of low-carbon materials and tracked embodied carbon across the entire build.
Central daylight atrium with living plant wall
Rooftop solar array and rainwater harvesting

GreenTech Headquarters now uses 40% less energy than a typical office of its size and gives employees a healthier, brighter place to work — proof that sustainable buildings can also be inspiring ones.

GreenTech Research Center is a dedicated innovation facility for GreenTech’s product development teams. The angular glass building houses laboratories, prototyping workshops, and collaboration spaces designed to accelerate clean-energy research.

A dramatic sloping glass roof floods the main research hall with daylight, while a concrete base houses specialist labs that require precise environmental control. Living green walls and an extensive green roof help regulate temperature and celebrate the client’s mission.

Following our successful delivery of GreenTech Headquarters, the client engaged Decode again for this technically complex facility. We coordinated specialist lab contractors and delivered strict environmental controls for sensitive research equipment.
Sloping structural glass roof over the main hall
Living green walls and extensive green roof
The Research Center gives GreenTech’s engineers a world-class environment for innovation — and strengthened a long-term partnership between our teams.

Historic Theater Renovation brought a 1920s performance venue back to life. Closed for over a decade, the 1,100-seat theater needed structural repairs, modern safety systems, and the careful restoration of its original decorative features.

The project balanced preservation with performance. Original plasterwork, gilding, and the proscenium arch were restored by heritage specialists, while new rigging, acoustics, accessibility upgrades, and back-of-house facilities prepared the venue for modern productions.

Decode served as principal contractor, working closely with heritage consultants and the city’s preservation office. We sequenced the work so that delicate restoration and heavy structural upgrades could happen safely side by side.
Restoration of original plasterwork and gilding
Seismic strengthening of the auditorium structure
New stage rigging and theatrical lighting systems
Full accessibility upgrades, including new lifts
Modern fire protection hidden within historic fabric
The theater reopened to sold-out audiences, its historic character intact and its systems ready for another century of performances. It’s one of the projects our team is proudest of.

Luxury Waterfront Residence is a four-bedroom lakeside home designed to make the most of its setting. Floor-to-ceiling glazing, cantilevered terraces, and a carefully orientated plan bring water views into every main room while protecting privacy from the shoreline path.

The 6,200 sq ft residence sits on a sloping waterfront lot that required careful engineering. A reinforced concrete podium anchors the home into the hillside, supporting a lightweight steel and timber upper level with a signature angled roofline and a rooftop terrace.

Decode delivered the project from design development through final handover. We managed geotechnical investigations, shoreline permits, and a tight construction window that avoided the lake’s seasonal restrictions — completing the home two weeks ahead of schedule.
Cantilevered terraces with frameless glass balustrades
Private boat dock and waterfront lounge
Smart home lighting, security, and climate control

The finished home blends seamlessly into its lakeside landscape while delivering the comfort, efficiency, and craftsmanship our client expected. It stands as a showcase of how thoughtful engineering can make a challenging site feel effortless.

Riverside Condominiums is a 140-unit residential development on a former industrial site along the river. The project transforms an underused stretch of waterfront into a vibrant community with homes, green space, and a public riverside walk.

Two mid-rise buildings step down toward the water, giving most units river views and generous private balconies. Shared amenities include a residents’ lounge, fitness center, landscaped courtyard, and secure underground parking.

We managed site remediation, flood-resilience works, and the full construction of both buildings. Careful phasing allowed the first building to be occupied while the second was completed, accelerating the client’s sales program.
Flood-resilient podium and raised ground floor
Public riverside walkway and landscaped courtyard
Riverside Condominiums turned a neglected industrial site into a thriving neighborhood. Residents enjoy river views and green space, and the community gained a new public waterfront to enjoy.

Summit Point Complex is a transformative development that combines office, retail, and green space in the heart of the business district. With 12 floors of flexible commercial space, ground-level retail, and a publicly accessible rooftop garden, it’s designed to promote urban vitality and work-life balance.

A bold exposed structural frame defines the building’s character while allowing column-free floor plates that tenants can configure freely. The rooftop garden offers planting, seating, and city views for office workers and the public alike.

As the primary contractor and construction manager, we provided end-to-end services, including site analysis, design coordination, budget management, and construction execution. We worked closely with stakeholders and the city to ensure compliance, safety, and excellence at every stage.
12 floors of flexible, column-free office space
High-efficiency HVAC with smart building controls
Summit Point Complex has become a landmark in the district — fully leased within a year of opening and a lively place where people work, shop, and relax.

Sustainable Community Park is a 12-acre public park built around a striking timber-and-steel pavilion. Designed with the local community, it offers green space, play areas, and an events venue built with low-impact materials.

The park’s sculptural pavilion hosts markets, performances, and community events, while surrounding landscapes include native planting, rain gardens, walking trails, and a natural play area. Every element was designed to manage stormwater on site and support biodiversity.

Decode delivered the pavilion structure, landscaping infrastructure, and site-wide drainage systems. We worked with local volunteers on planting days and kept large sections of the park open throughout construction.
Rain gardens and on-site stormwater management
Natural play area built from reclaimed materials
The park has become a favorite gathering place for the whole community — a green, resilient public space that shows how sustainable design and great architecture can go hand in hand.

The Keystone Residences is a luxury residential development featuring 85 high-end condominium units across two contemporary mid-rise towers. Designed with urban elegance and sustainability in mind, it offers refined living close to the city center.

Distinctive vertical fins give the towers their signature look while shading the facades from the summer sun. Inside, residents enjoy smart-home integration, premium finishes, rooftop amenities, and energy-efficient systems throughout.

We handled the full design and construction process, from pre-construction planning and permitting to final execution. Our team coordinated with architects, engineers, and local agencies to ensure timely delivery and top-tier quality.
Underground parking with EV charging stations
The Keystone Residences sold out before completion. The project shows how thoughtful design, quality materials, and disciplined construction management create homes that residents are proud to own.

No two homes are the same, and neither are two renovations. We tailor the scope, schedule, and sequence of work to your household — phasing rooms so you can keep living at home, or completing everything in one efficient push when you’re away.
